evals.prompt: Design a polished one-page landing page for AtlasOps, a B2B incident-command SaaS for infrastructure teams. Audience: SRE leaders and platform engineering managers. Tone: modern minimal / tech utility. Include hero, proof, feature modules, workflow section, pricing teaser, and final CTA. Build a complete standalone HTML file.
evals.expected_output: A standalone HTML landing page with a coherent software-native visual system, inspectable sections, responsive CSS, specific AtlasOps copy, trustworthy proof handling, and a working decision path.
expectations: The output directory contains at least one non-empty runnable HTML file.
The HTML uses unique meaningful data-od-id attributes on core visible sections or controls.
The HTML defines a tokenized visual system using CSS custom properties and at least one oklch() color.
The landing page includes specific AtlasOps/SRE/incident-command copy rather than lorem ipsum or Feature One style filler.
The HTML includes responsive implementation evidence such as @media, clamp(), container queries, or mobile layout CSS.
Claims, proof, metrics, customer quotes, or certifications are not fabricated as factual evidence.
The primary CTA has a real visible response or viable destination rather than a dead clickable-looking control.
The output avoids obvious AI-slop defaults: emoji feature icons, generic purple gradients, and equal rounded cards with left-border accent strips.
The execution transcript shows that the artifact was rendered or browser-checked when browser tooling was available.

evals.prompt: Make a 6-slide HTML deck for a climate-finance board update called 'Carbon Ledger Q3'. Audience: board members. Style: editorial but restrained. Slides: title, market context, portfolio movement, risk map, operating plan, decision ask. Build a complete standalone HTML deck.
evals.expected_output: A standalone six-slide HTML board deck with fixed-canvas mechanics, board-ready editorial content, evidence-aware claims, presentation navigation, and verified legibility.
expectations: The output directory contains at least one non-empty runnable HTML file.
The HTML contains exactly six slide sections or equivalent slide containers matching the requested narrative.
Each slide is labeled with data-screen-label or an equivalent 1-indexed semantic slide label.
The deck includes keyboard navigation, a visible counter, print styles, and localStorage position persistence.
The deck uses a fixed-canvas or scale-to-fit presentation structure such as 1920x1080, aspect-ratio 16/9, or a stage wrapper.
The slide content is specific to Carbon Ledger Q3 climate-finance board reporting, not generic business filler.
Unknown portfolio metrics or market claims are labeled honestly rather than presented as invented facts.
The decision-ask slide contains a concrete board decision rather than a generic closing CTA.
The execution transcript shows that navigation and rendered slide legibility were checked when browser tooling was available.

evals.prompt: Create a mobile onboarding prototype for a food delivery app named BentoLoop. Include at least three screens: welcome, dietary preferences, and live order tracking. Target iOS. Style: human and approachable. Build a complete standalone HTML file with clickable navigation between screens.
evals.expected_output: A standalone iOS mobile prototype with framed screens, real onboarding and tracking state transitions, accessible touch targets, and an approachable BentoLoop visual system.
expectations: The output directory contains at least one non-empty runnable HTML file.
The HTML includes at least three distinct BentoLoop onboarding or order-tracking screens/states.
The prototype includes appropriate iOS framing evidence such as a status area, Dynamic Island, safe-area bottom affordance, or iPhone frame without covering content.
The HTML includes working clickable navigation or JavaScript state transitions between the requested screens.
Primary mobile controls have at least 44px target sizing and meaningful accessible names.
The content is specific to food delivery, dietary preferences, and live order tracking rather than generic app-placeholder text.
The order-tracking screen communicates progress/state and a useful next action, not only a static map illustration.
The execution transcript shows that the mobile flow was exercised in a rendered browser when browser tooling was available.

evals.prompt: Build a standalone HTML product console for RelayGrid, a batch-job scheduler used by platform operators. The primary task is diagnosing and recovering failed jobs. Include dense job navigation, a job table, a failed-job detail drawer, and explicit simulations for loading, filter-empty, API error, permission-limited, queued, running, failed, retrying, and recovered states. Retry must visibly transition from failed to retrying to recovered. Destructive cancellation must explain consequences. Do not ask questions; use a dense operational direction.
evals.expected_output: A dense operational console whose main task is failure diagnosis and recovery, with complete non-happy states, semantic job status, a functional retry path, and browser-verified interactions.
expectations: The output directory contains at least one non-empty runnable HTML file.
The first viewport makes failed-job diagnosis and recovery the obvious primary task rather than presenting a generic KPI card wall.
The artifact provides reachable simulations or visible UI for loading, filter-empty, API error, permission-limited, queued, running, failed, retrying, and recovered states.
The failed-job detail exposes a concrete failure reason and a recovery action tied to the selected job.
Retry visibly transitions through a pending/retrying state and then a recovered or successful state.
Permission-limited actions are unavailable with an explanation rather than silently enabled.
Destructive cancellation identifies the affected job and explains the consequence before confirmation.
Status, risk, category, and actions are not all represented as interchangeable decorative pills.
The layout includes responsive behavior and meaningful data-od-id attributes.
The execution transcript shows browser rendering plus interaction checks for the failed-job drawer and retry path when browser tooling was available.

evals.prompt: Create a standalone interactive HTML prototype for TracePilot, an AI incident postmortem assistant. The experience must let an SRE specify service, time range, and evidence sources; show understanding, clarification, execution, waiting-for-user, failed, and completed states; require explicit confirmation before publishing a postmortem; present evidence-backed findings with uncertainty; and allow edit scope, cancel, retry, and resume. Do not expose chain-of-thought. Use controlled product UI rather than making the whole product a chat transcript.
evals.expected_output: An agentic workflow prototype that makes intent, context, runtime state, decision checkpoints, evidence, uncertainty, and recovery visible through controlled product UI.
expectations: The output directory contains at least one non-empty runnable HTML file.
The intent entry visibly includes service, time range, and evidence-source context rather than only a freeform chat box.
The artifact provides reachable or visible understanding, clarification, execution, waiting-for-user, failed, and completed states.
Publishing is blocked behind an explicit confirmation that identifies what will be published and its scope.
Findings distinguish evidence, inference/recommendation, and uncertainty without fabricated citations or confidence scores.
The user can edit scope, cancel, retry, and resume through controls connected to the workflow state.
The primary experience uses controlled cards, panels, or structured surfaces rather than rendering the entire product as an undifferentiated chat transcript.
The artifact does not expose hidden reasoning or chain-of-thought as a trust mechanism.
The execution transcript shows browser rendering and at least one decision/recovery path check when browser tooling was available.

Add a failed-job detail drawer with error evidence and a retry flow that visibly transitions through pending to recovered. Keep the existing table and filters. Copy the updated runnable files into the output directory. Do not create a parallel app, independent palette, or competing token system.
evals.expected_output: A surgical revision of the supplied QueueScope console that preserves the design authority and existing structure while adding a functional failure-recovery flow.
expectations: The output directory contains an updated runnable QueueScope HTML artifact.
The established app shell, existing table, and filters remain present rather than being replaced by a new application.
The revision reuses the supplied semantic CSS variables and does not introduce an independent palette or competing token system.
The new failed-job drawer is tied to the selected row and displays error evidence.
Retry visibly transitions through pending/retrying to recovered and updates the selected job state.
The compact geometry and typography rules from DESIGN.md remain visibly and structurally respected.
No unrelated landing-page hero, demo settings panel, or broad visual redesign is introduced.
The execution transcript shows the supplied design authority was inspected before editing and the updated flow was browser-checked when browser tooling was available.
